Subject: Sutherland Labs — on-prem landing zone inventory & service matrix

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I've attached a lightweight inventory template to capture the minimal facts we need for an on-prem Private deployment (node types, disk classes, networking zones, and who owns the racks). Could you please populate the sheet and return it by EOB Friday?

High-level asks for the inventory:
- Physical hosts / rack IDs where you expect Redwood nodes to land.
- Expected pod categories: inference (GPU), classifier (CPU-heavy), control-plane/management (small, HA), and batch/offline.
- Disk types per host (NVMe local, SAS SSD, SAN iSCSI) and whether encryption-at-rest is required by policy.
- Network connectivity: internal VLANs, egress NAT, internet breakout IPs, and whether you'll allow pod egress to (s3.redwood.ai) or need a proxy.
- Any existing NFS/SMB exports we should avoid; preferred block-store for PVs.

A few notes from our side:
- For inference pods we typically recommend a dedicated node pool with 4–8 GPUs to start for a PoC (we can right-size after profiling).
- We'll bring a CSI manifest and a small operator to manage ephemeral caches; if you prefer a cluster-level sidecar for KV caching we can adjust.
- For control plane we recommend 3 management nodes in a separate management VLAN with floating IPs — happy to run through HA options.

Attachments: sutherland-node-inventory.xlsx (xlsx)

If anything in the sheet is sensitive, you can send it to the itops alias and cc me. I'll schedule an internal tech workshop after I get the inventory so Ben and Aditya can map a deployment matrix.

Best,

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear template. We've filled the high-level inventory and attached a zone diagram showing our rack layout and VLANs. A couple of immediate clarifications from our infra team:

- GPUs: we have two racks with 4x A40-class nodes each (PCIe), plus a smaller pool of 2 x T4 hosts for low-priority work. Trying to avoid any noisy-neighbor issues.
- Storage: Primary is a SAN (iSCSI) served by NetStore; NVMe is available locally on nodes but we plan to reserve local NVMe for ephemeral caches only.
- Encryption: We require envelope encryption for any persistent store holding customer data; metadata-only stores can be plaintext.
- Egress: Outbound HTTPS is allowed but must go through our corporate proxy (proxy.corp.sutherland:3128).

Attached: zone-network-diagram.pdf

We can do a tech workshop next Tuesday afternoon (PST).

Emily — thanks for the upload and the diagram, that's very helpful. I pulled a few items from your answers and added short recommendations inline below.

1) GPU node pool sizing
- Given two racks with 4 A40-class nodes each, recommend initial nodepool: inference-gpu (taint: inference=true:NoSchedule), 4 nodes, each with 1–2 GPUs dedicated to Redwood pods. Start with pod limits to avoid scheduling contention: requests: 1 GPU, limits: 1 GPU per pod.
- Use topologySpreadConstraints to keep replicas across racks for failure domain isolation.

2) Local NVMe vs SAN
- Use local NVMe for ephemeral KV caches and sharded KV stores (much faster for token cache).
- For persistent model storage and checkpoints use NetStore iSCSI-backed PVs with a StorageClass that enforces rwx=false, encryption (if required), and reclaimPolicy: Retain. We will supply a short CSI shim to support resize and snapshots if your SAN supports it.

3) Network / egress via proxy
- Our runtime can be configured to route outbound calls through an HTTP proxy — we will provide env var and init container settings.
- Recommend a service account for operator egress with a network-policy permitting traffic only to the proxy endpoint.

4) Control plane and HA
- Management nodes in separate VLAN are good. We'll deploy kubeadm-style control plane with 3 control-plane VMs and keep kubelet TLS rotated via our operator.

5) Secrets / KMS
- For envelope encryption we integrate with customer KMS over HTTPS. Please confirm whether you can host a Vault endpoint internally or if we should point at AWS KMS over a VPN.

Attachments: redwood-mop-deploy-checklist.md (md) — contains the operational steps we run during on-prem cluster provisioning (inventory validation, CSI install, node labeling, role binding).

Next steps:
- Marissa: can you lock a 90-min slot for the tech workshop Tuesday 14:00–15:30 PST?
- Emily: confirm whether you'll host an internal KMS endpoint or want a VPN to cloud KMS.

Cheers,

Emily — quick follow from my side ahead of Tuesday's workshop. A few concrete config snippets so your infra team can eyeball them beforehand:

- Node labels & taints example:
  kubectl label node node-01 node-role.kubernetes.io/inference=worker
  kubectl taint nodes node-01 inference=true:NoSchedule

- StorageClass example (iSCSI, encrypted):
  apiVersion: storage.k8s.io/v1
  kind: StorageClass
  metadata:
    name: netstore-enc
  provisioner: csi.netstore.company.com
  parameters:
    encryption: \"true\"
    fsType: ext4
  reclaimPolicy: Retain
  volumeBindingMode: WaitForFirstConsumer

- CSI note: we'll request a small privileged DaemonSet to handle attach/detach on the hosts (single binary, logs to /var/log/redwood-csi.log).

Operational asks from Sutherland before we hit staging:
- Confirm a BMC/IPMI access window for two hosts so we can validate bootstrapping in your environment.
- Provide a test object store endpoint behind the proxy for initial model pulls.

Emily — could you confirm the proxy test URL and whether we have IPMI access to the two nodes in rack B?

Emily replied: \"Confirm IPMI on rack-B nodes is on the ticket — we enabled outbound to proxy.corp.sutherland:3128 and uploaded the inventory to the Drive. See you Tuesday.\"
